blocks.text: Managing multiple Chrome profiles for evaluation projects

Evaluation projects often require you to use different accounts or maintain specific browser settings. Creating a separate Chrome profile is the most effective way to keep your environment clean. Go to your profile icon in the top right of the browser window. Select Add to create a new profile. This keeps your search history, bookmarks, and extensions isolated. You can even assign a different color theme to each profile to distinguish your evaluation work from your personal browsing.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for faster rating

Efficiency in evaluation comes down to how quickly you can move between tabs and windows. Learn these core shortcuts to reduce your reliance on the trackpad. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab instantly. Use ⌘ + L to jump directly to the address bar for a new search. If you need to close a tab quickly, use ⌘ + W. To reopen a tab you closed by accident, use ⌘ + ⇧ + T. These small movements save significant time over a long shift.
Keeping your browser stable for evaluation tasks

Browser performance is critical when you are labeling hundreds of passages in a single shift. Chrome on Mac performs best when you keep your extension list minimal. Only install tools that you use for every single task. If you experience lag or page loading errors, check your extensions in Chrome > Window > Extensions. Disable anything you do not need. Clearing your browsing data is also a standard fix for persistent issues. Go to Chrome > Clear Browsing Data to remove cached images and files that might be interfering with site rendering.

If a site refuses to load or shows a broken layout, clear the cache for that specific site rather than your entire history. Use the site settings menu in the address bar to manage site-specific permissions and storage.

blocks.text: How Lazur assists with search engine evaluation

Lazur acts as your assistant while you work in Chrome. When you are stuck on a complex rating task, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur for help. You can ask for a quick summary of a long article or have it clarify a specific guideline. Lazur does not click buttons for you, but it can point at specific elements on your screen to help you find what you need. If you need to write a rationale, hold fn and dictate your thoughts directly into the text box. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the task.

To keep your tools working, ensure your Mac is running macOS 13 Ventura or later. This is the minimum requirement for the current version of Chrome. Check your version by going to Chrome > About Google Chrome. If you are on an older version, the browser will prompt you to update. Keeping your browser updated is not just about features. It ensures you have the latest security patches required by many evaluation platforms.

Most evaluators manage their own invoices and project communications. Use Chrome profiles to keep your project management portal separate from your evaluation tabs. If you use a spreadsheet to track your hours, keep it pinned in a dedicated window. Right-click the tab and select Pin to keep it at the front of your tab bar. This prevents you from accidentally closing it during a busy session.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Chrome browser?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your entire Mac, including inside Chrome. It can see the content of your browser tabs and help you with research or text input.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to automate my rating tasks?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, fill out forms, or operate your rating portal. It is designed to help you research, write, and find information faster.

faq.question: How do I clear my cache in Chrome on Mac?
faq.answer: Go to the Chrome menu, select Clear Browsing Data, choose your time range, and ensure Cached images and files is checked before clicking Clear data.

faq.question: Why does Chrome feel slow on my Mac?
faq.answer: Slow performance is often caused by too many open tabs, too many active extensions, or a corrupted cache. Try closing unused tabs or disabling unnecessary extensions.
